name: Montana
feeText: Clerk of district court fee for filing a petition for dissolution of marriage, $170; each defendant or respondent pays $60 on appearance (Mont. Code Ann. § 25-1-201(1)(a)-(b), 2025 MCA).

otherFees.what: Entry of judgment, from the prevailing party (§ 25-1-201(1)(c))

waiver.name: Affidavit and financial statement requesting a waiver of fees (Mont. Code Ann. § 25-10-404)

residency.text: One party must have been domiciled in Montana, or stationed there in the armed services, for 90 days before filing (Mont. Code Ann. § 40-4-104(1)(a)).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period for a regular dissolution was found. Irretrievable breakdown is shown by living separate and apart for more than 180 days before filing or by serious marital discord (§ 40-4-104(1)(b)). In a summary dissolution the hearing is held after 20 days from the filing of the joint petition (§ 40-4-133).

simplified.text: Summary dissolution on a joint petition (Mont. Code Ann. §§ 40-4-130 to 40-4-136): irreconcilable differences, wife not pregnant, no children or an agreed parenting plan with support already ordered, no real property (short residential leases excepted), unsecured marital debts not over $20,000, assets under $50,000, signed division agreement, maintenance waived; hearing after 20 days.

uncertain: Montana Code read on archive.legmt.gov (the Legislature's official MCA archive site, 2025 MCA).
Other statutory surcharges collected with a dissolution filing outside § 25-1-201 were not checked; filingFee is the § 25-1-201(1)(a) amount only.
Parenting class: no statewide statute read; a Montana Judicial Branch court-sanctioned education program for dissolution exists per an archived courts.mt.gov policy file, but it was not read.
Waiver form title on courts.mt.gov not read; the statute is cited instead.
separationRequiredDays null: the 180-day separation is one of two ways to prove irretrievable breakdown.
